method: WebSearch retrieval. Items marked 'quote' appeared word-for-word in WebSearch output; 'paraphrase'/'stat (paraphrased)' faithfully restate content the search tool returned from the cited source.
angle_summary: Systematic 'life-admin' failure driven by time blindness, prospective memory deficits, and 'out of sight, out of mind' working-memory lapses. Measurable fallout: 60-90% higher missed-GP-appointment rates, 57% missing loan payments, chronic lateness affecting up to 80%, involuntary 'ghosting', wasted food, lapsed prescriptions. Standard fixes fail because ADHD brains habituate to static alarms and abandon apps once novelty wears off. Emotional cost severe: shame-avoidance cycles amplified by RSD, partners absorbing the mental load, ~2x divorce rates.

problems.name: Time blindness: hours vanish, chronically late, 'waiting mode' eats whole days
problems.frequency_signal: Up to 80% of adults with ADHD reportedly struggle with time management/punctuality; one-third of 1,859 surveyed adults said time-management problems contribute the greatest stress to their lives.

evidence.text: ADDitude surveyed 1,859 adults with ADHD, one-third of whom said that problems with time management and productivity contribute the greatest amount of stress to their lives.
Studies have shown that up to 80% of adults with ADHD struggle with time management and punctuality issues.

In 'waiting mode', a person can't start anything before an appointment — accomplishing nothing despite 6 hours available — because past experiences of missing appointments make not-starting feel safer than losing track of time.
Time blindness linked to reduced prefrontal cortex activation and dopamine pathway irregularities; hours pass as if minutes ('time agnosia') during hyperfocus.

problems.existing_solutions: Visual timers (Time Timer ~$35-45), Pomodoro apps, time-blocking, planner apps.
problems.gap: Visual timers useless during hyperfocus; single-beep timers dismissed as 'not urgent'; ticking countdowns trigger time anxiety. Nothing bridges 'felt time' contextually or addresses waiting-mode paralysis.

problems.name: Forgotten bills and the compounding 'ADHD tax'
problems.frequency_signal: 57% of people with ADHD miss loan payments; default rates grow exponentially by middle age; projected lifetime income deficit of $1.27M vs controls.

evidence.text: According to Reuters, 57% of people with ADHD miss loan payments, more than half have a bad credit rating, and 71% have not saved for retirement; 62% shop impulsively.

People with ADHD start adulthood with normal credit demand and default rates, but in middle age their default rates grow exponentially; by age 30 the earnings trajectory projected a lifetime income deficit of $1.27 million vs controls.
evidence.source: Science Advances — 'ADHD, financial distress, and suicide in adulthood: A population study'

evidence.text: In a 2020 study of nearly 1,300 people, only 20% of adults with ADHD had saved for retirement vs 42% of neurotypical peers; ADHD symptoms correlate with carried credit balances, late payments, and pawn-service use.
evidence.source: PMC — Financial decision-making in a community sample

evidence.text: People report entering car registration numbers wrong (parking fines) and not noticing council tax direct debits had stopped for over a year.

problems.existing_solutions: Autopay, recurring calendar reminders, budgeting apps, ADHD-money coaching content.
problems.gap: Autopay fails for one-off invoices, renewals, mailed notices, anything requiring a decision. No tool watches the whole obligation surface and escalates only what will actually cost money if ignored.

problems.name: Missed appointments and prospective-memory failures
problems.frequency_signal: 60-90% more likely to miss GP appointments (n=2,453 vs 12,200 controls); 38% miss at least one GP appointment annually; forgetfulness is the #1 reason for medication non-adherence (39%).

evidence.text: Patients with ADHD (Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder) are 60-90 percent more likely to miss appointments with their doctors, compared to the general population
Annually 38% of those age ≥18 years missed at least one GP appointment.
Individuals with ADHD showed clear deficits in everyday prospective memory performance, recalling and executing fewer of their own real-life intentions than controls.
evidence.source: PLOS One — Complex Prospective Memory in Adults with ADHD

evidence.text: Up to 80% of adults prescribed ADHD medications fail to adhere within the first year; an Express Scripts pilot of 600,000 patients identified forgetfulness as the single largest reason for non-adherence at 39%.

problems.existing_solutions: Clinic SMS reminders, calendar apps, pill organizers, episodic-future-thinking interventions (research stage).
problems.gap: Clinic reminders arrive on the clinic's schedule, not at the actionable moment; no consumer product closes the loop from 'reminder seen' to 'left the house on time' (transit-aware, escalating, confirmation-seeking).

problems.name: Involuntary ghosting: unanswered texts, emails, and inbox avoidance
problems.frequency_signal: Named community phenomena ('involuntary ghosting', 'the 2-second or 2-week response pattern') with dedicated content across Inflow, Mini ADHD Coach, Klarity, therapy practices.

evidence.text: 'Involuntary ghosting': people with ADHD forget to respond to texts; as unanswered messages pile up so does guilt — a negative feedback loop devastating to self-esteem; friends stop reaching out and good friendships fade away.

Task initiation makes even a simple reply hard to start; time blindness turns 'in a minute' into days; out of sight slips completely out of attention; messages carrying pressure become emotionally overwhelming to open.
With mail avoidance, bills go unpaid, tickets and taxes gather interest, credit goes down, services get cut off, invitations missed; every glance at the unopened stack brings dread.
Every unopened email represents a potential obligation and possible failure; rejection sensitivity causes shame over delayed responses; a mixed inbox triggers avoidance rather than action.

problems.existing_solutions: Email cleanup tools, snooze features, pinned messages, coping-strategy content.
problems.gap: Generic tools organize but don't resurface human obligations (the friend's text from 9 days ago, the RSVP); nothing distinguishes shame-blocked replies from forgotten ones or drafts the low-friction way back in. The social-repair layer is entirely unserved.

problems.name: Reminder habituation: alarms and apps stop working within weeks
problems.frequency_signal: Described as universal across ADHD reminder guides; app abandonment a recurring theme; even ADHD-specific app makers acknowledge single-point notifications fail.

evidence.text: ADHD brains filter out alarms via executive dysfunction, cue desensitisation, and emotional overload: the notification sound that once jolted you into action now barely registers; visual cues become invisible wallpaper — the brain has habituated.

Standard phone reminders are not effective on their own for most people with ADHD: single-point notifications are easily dismissed due to alarm fatigue, timing mismatches, and the micro-decision problem; a reminder every 10 minutes causes you to ignore them all.
A timer that beeps once is easy to dismiss during hyperfocus — the brain categorizes the sound as 'not urgent'; for some, ticking countdowns trigger time anxiety rather than awareness.

problems.existing_solutions: Layered/escalating reminders, varied tones, persistent until-done alerts, smart-home cues, proof-of-action alarm apps.
problems.gap: No mainstream product implements anti-habituation as a core mechanic: rotating modalities/voices/channels, salience calibrated to consequence, confirmation that the ACTION (not the dismissal) happened, detection of stale cues.

problems.name: Mental-load offloading and the shame spiral: relationships absorb the failure
problems.frequency_signal: 96% of 700 surveyed spouses say ADHD makes household management harder; ~2x divorce rates (50-60% vs ~30%); 38% report being 'close to divorce'.

evidence.text: ADHD-affected couples have a divorce rate 2x higher than the general population (around 50-60% vs 30%); 38% of ADHD couples report being 'close to divorce'; a survey of 700 ADHD partners found 96% of spouses say ADHD makes household management harder.

The partner without ADHD absorbs planning, reminding, follow-through while the ADHD partner faces a steady stream of correction — one feels like a manager, the other a perpetual disappointment; resentment builds while shame grows.

Repeated prospective-memory failures create a shame cycle that mimics depression — every missed date reinforces 'I am a bad friend/partner/child'; partners interpret forgotten dates as evidence of not caring.
Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria amplifies the emotional pain of perceived criticism, exacerbating shame and leading to self-criticism, anxiety, and depression.

problems.existing_solutions: Couples therapy, medication + CBT, shared calendars, written finance agreements, body-doubling apps (Dubbii: 500k+ users; Focusmate, FLOWN).
problems.gap: Every mitigation either bills by the hour or quietly re-installs the partner as project manager. No neutral third party holds the mental load itself — tracking obligations, doing the nagging, confirming completion — so neither partner has to be the parent.
